about.title: Personal Injury Help in Clovis, California
about.longDescription: Clovis sits just northeast of Fresno, and much of daily life here runs along a handful of busy corridors. Shaw Avenue, Herndon Avenue, Clovis Avenue, and W Shaw Avenue carry the highest public-record collision counts in the city. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, Clovis logged 356 injury collisions, with 509 people hurt and 1 traffic death. Reports tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when the end-of-week commute and errand traffic overlap. Whether your injury happened in a car near Old Town Clovis, on a bike along a neighborhood street, or in a fall at a local shop, the questions afterward tend to be the same: who pays for treatment, how do you deal with the insurer, and what happens to the income you are missing. LawProactive exists to make the next step simple. We are a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases in Fresno County, and we never charge you for that connection. The attorney you speak with works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened; we help you find someone who can review it. It costs you nothing to start.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Clovis Claim

items.title: The clock is two years, sometimes less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, the window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to talk with an attorney early.

items.title: Partial fault does not shut you out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you were partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by your share, but you are not barred from pursuing a claim.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering in ordinary cases
items.desc: California does not limit non-economic damages in typical injury cases. That means the attorney can account for the full effect the injury has had on your daily life, not just your medical bills.

items.title: Attorneys work on contingency
items.desc: The independent attorneys in our network do not charge hourly fees. They are paid only if there is a recovery, so cost should never be the reason you wait.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, the deadline is two years from the date of injury. If your claim is against a government entity, such as a city or county agency, you may have only six months to file a required notice. An attorney can confirm which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system. Your recovery is reduced by whatever percentage of fault is assigned to you, but you can still pursue a claim even if you share some blame. This is one of the reasons it is worth having an attorney review the details before assuming you have no options.
